items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: He was the first high note trumpet player that Lunceford had before Paul Webster was Stevenson.

ctx.x: It must have been '31, '32 -- '31, '30 because I went with Earl Hines right after that. Jimmy Mundy was the first guy to go with Earl Hines. But I'll tell you how this kind of came about. We used to play a battle of music all the time with a band from Baltimore, and this band was called the Ambassadors.

Now, in this band there was a trumpet player, high note trumpet player. He was very flashy, and his name was Stevenson. But he went with Lunceford later on. He was the first high note trumpet player that Lunceford had before Paul Webster was Stevenson. He went with -- Tommy was a fantastic trumpet player. Played a lot of high
notes. And he was with Lunceford when he got popular in New York at the Cotton Club, Thommy was, and nice looking boy. He was a fantastic trumpet player.
